{{Short description|Austrian research scientist (1928–1989)}}

'''Manfred "Fred" Kochen''' (4 July 1928 – 7 January 1989) was an Austrian research scientist and professor. He is best known for his academic work and research career with various companies, including [[IBM]]. Kochen's research emphasized [[mathematics]], [[information science]] and [[behavioural sciences]] research, as well as early studies of concepts in the field of [[artificial intelligence]], where he questioned the possibility of [[artificial general intelligence]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Garfield |first=Eugene |date=June 19, 1989 |title=Manfred Kochen: In Memory of an Information Scientist Pioneer qua World Brain-ist |url=https://garfield.library.upenn.edu/essays/v12p166y1989.pdf |journal=Current Comments |volume=12 |pages=3 |via=University of Pennsylvania Libraries}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kochen |first=Manfred |date=June 1, 1985 |title=The future of AI and human flexibility |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.3233/HSM-1985-5209?_gl=1*1she2av*_up*MQ..*_ga*NTA4ODY3NzIyLjE3NzU4MzgzODg.*_ga_60R758KFDG*czE3NzU4MzgzODgkbzEkZzAkdDE3NzU4MzgzODgkajYwJGwwJGgxMTE5NjgxOTU0 |journal=Human Systems Management |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=159–162 |doi=10.3233/HSM-1985-5209 |via=SagePub}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Manfred Kochen was born on 4 July 1928, in [[Vienna]], Austria. Some time before the outbreak of [[World War II]], his family fled [[Europe]] to escape the threat of Nazi persecution, escaping via [[Portugal]].<ref name=":0" />

Prior to 1947, Manfred Kochen moved to the [[United States]], where he attended Brooklyn Technical High School, graduating with a Mechanical Course diploma. Kochen received his Bachelor's of Science from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in Cambridge, Massachusetts in 1950, with a concentration in [[physics]].<ref name=":0" /> Kochen would subsequently go on to [[Columbia University]], where he would receive both his Master of Arts and PhD in [[applied mathematics]] in 1951 and 1955 respectively.<ref name=":0" />  During his doctoral studies, he served as an analyst with the John von Neumann project at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] with [[Princeton University]].<ref name=":0" /> After earning his doctorate, Kochen also served as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Harvard University]] and the  [[University of Cambridge]].

Kochen met his wife, Paula, in New York City. They were married from 1954 until his death.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
After concluding his postdoctoral research, Kochen began working as a research scientist at IBM's [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center]], where he worked until 1964.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Zeleny |first=Milan |date=1989-06-01 |title=Manfred Kochen (1928–1989) |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.3233/HSM-1989-8202 |journal=Human Systems Management |volume=8 |issue=2 |pages=95–96 |doi=10.3233/HSM-1989-8202}}</ref> In 1965, he began teaching at the [[University of Michigan Medicine|University of Michigan School of Medicine]] as a professor of information science, while he also held simultaneous posts as an adjunct professor in the [[Ross School of Business]], as well as acting as a research mathematician in the [[Mental Health Research Institute (Michigan)]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

In 1972, Kochen was elevated to a full professorship, and would continue to teach until his death.<ref name=":0" />

Kochen died on 7 January 1989. His death was reported in the [[Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology|Journal of the American Society for Information Science]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gordon |first1=Michael |last2=Blair |first2=David |last3=Lindsay |first3=Robert |date=July 1989 |title=Manfred Kochen 1928-1989: Remembrances of a scholar and a gentle man |url=https://doi.org/10.1002/(sici)1097-4571(198907)40:4<223::aid-asi1>3.0.co;2-i |journal=Journal of the American Society for Information Science |volume=40 |issue=4 |pages=223–225 |doi=10.1002/(sici)1097-4571(198907)40:4<223::aid-asi1>3.0.co;2-i |issn=0002-8231|url-access=subscription }}</ref> notices of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=March 1989 |title=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/198903/198903FullIssue.pdf?adat=March%201989&trk=&cat=none&type=.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=326 |via=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> and his legacy was analyzed by [[Don R. Swanson]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Swanson |first=Don R. |date=1990-01-01 |title=Integrative mechanisms in the growth of knowledge: A legacy of Manfred Kochen∗ |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0306-4573%2890%2990005-M |journal=Information Processing & Management |series=Special Issue: Natural Language Processing and Information Retrieval |volume=26 |issue=1 |pages=9–16 |doi=10.1016/0306-4573(90)90005-M |issn=0306-4573|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
